Stress and intonation are important parts of both listening and speaking in English. There are four different types of stress. Let's focus on emphatic stress.
When you decide to emphasize something, you can change the stress from the main noun to another content word such as an adjective (small, highest) or adverb (very, extremely).
This emphasis focuses the listener's attention to the extraordinary quality of what you want to emphasize.

That was a hard question. - Standard statement
That was a hard question. - Emphasizes how hard the question was.
It is common to use emphatic stress with adverbs like:
That was an extremely hard question.
Remember, when you stress a word, your intonation rises and the word is said slightly longer and louder than the other words.

Stress with Suffixes: One Syllable Before the Suffix

Sometimes, stressed syllables based on suffixes appear to not follow any pattern at all.
But, when you look at words in reverse, from the end of the word toward the front, a pattern emerges.
These patterns can help you become familiar with how certain words are pronounced.

For instance, the words classic, specific, and economic all include the -ic suffix. They are stressed on the first, second, and third syllables, respectively. The stress patterns can only be found when it is understood that syllables must be counted from the end of the word toward the beginning of the word. In fact, the words classic, specific, and economic all follow the same pattern of being stressed on the syllable before the -ic suffix.

Let's look at the words classic, specific and economic. They all end in the suffix -ic. When you read them aloud, they do not necessarily follow a pattern. But, try looking at them in reverse. You will notice a pattern.

images.text:
Located in the southwest section of China, the nation of Tibet is the highest region on Earth, with an elevation that averages over 16,000 feet or 4,875 meters in metric. Because it is so high up, Tibet is sometimes called the "roof of the world."
One of the highest plateaus is a portion of Tibet called the Chang Tang, or northern plateau. This is home to the Changpa nomads, a semi-nomadic Tibetan ethnic group. Here they live their stoic lives, leading their heavy coated goats, sheep, and yaks from pasture to pasture, and singing their traditional music.

Living on the Chang Tang, surviving temperatures that can change by 80 degrees Fahrenheit in one day and that can go as low as minus 40 degrees Fahrenheit in the winter seems to defy logic, but they manage it.
Tibet has a unique and ancient culture that dates back hundreds of years. In the 7th century AD, Buddhists came to Tibet on a mission to spread their religion. They had vision. They had created an alphabet for the Tibetan language, then translated the Buddhist holy books into a Tibetan version. Buddhism thrived.

The entry of Buddhism into Tibet led to the development of Lamaism, Tibet's spiritual movement. The Dalai Lama, the man who leads the movement with passion, is believed to be the reincarnation of the Buddha. When a Dalai Lama dies, his soul is thought to enter the body of a newborn boy who then becomes the next Dalai Lama.
